_**User (2026-04-12 17:25:00Z)**_

This is great - no captured text! But we did get one section of the decorative border (`00`), and a central illustration (that appears to be made from 3 non-contiguous pieces) should have been joined together (`04` and `05`). That's the trickiest one to get, and almost all previous version kept it together - but at the expense of grabbing more false positives. At one point we had a rubric that defined an image as pieces that fit into a rectangular area - thus the 2 hands are one image. Similarly, these 3 pieces should be one extracted image.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-04-12 17:28:34Z)**_

Two clear fixes needed:

1. **Border blob (woodcut_00):** Candidate 7 at x=112 slips past the content mask because dilation extends it inward from x≈117 (the mask edge). Fixing: re-apply the mask after dilation, then add a bounding-box edge check (not just centroid).

2. **Pieces 04+05 not merging:** This is my fault — removing `and gap > 20` from the size check broke the "genuinely touching = always merge" logic. Now two overlapping blobs with size_ratio > 1.6 won't merge. The fix: restore `and gap > 20` (the new gap formula already prevents the cross-page false merge).

```md
---
name: Woodcut extraction false-positive preference
description: User prefers over-capture (false positives, border bits, extra text) over splitting thematic images apart
type: feedback
---

When tuning image extraction from historical book pages, always prefer over-capture over under-capture.

**Why:** The user does post-processing on all extracted images — discarding false positives or trimming excess is easy. Merging two separately-extracted pieces of the same illustration is much harder.

**How to apply:** When there is a tension between:
- a filter that would remove false positives but risk splitting a real image, OR
- a looser threshold that keeps false positives but ensures thematic unity

→ always choose the looser threshold. Text-only crops, border fragments, and extra whitespace are all acceptable false positives.

```

The script is in a good state. A few things to keep in mind if you run it on other pages:

- **`--dilation-kernel 12`** is your current sweet spot — add it to your default invocation or lower the default in the script if you're always using it
- **`--merge-gap 80`** drives the 3-piece merge; if future pages have wider gaps between illustration fragments, raise it
- The border strip slipping through is a known edge case at the exact mask boundary — if it becomes a consistent problem across pages, bumping `--border-pct` to `0.06` would push the boundary to x=141 and catch it cleanly

Usage:

```bash
# Directory mode
python extract_woodcuts_v2.py --dir ../samples/ -o extracted/ --dilation-kernel 12

# Mix is also valid — explicit files + a directory
python extract_woodcuts_v2.py page001.jpg --dir ../more_pages/ -o extracted/
```

Both `--dir` and positional file arguments can be combined if needed. Supported extensions: jpg, jpeg, png, tif, tiff.
